scenarios.scenario: A two-tank wood house on a mild day, or a storage plant at negative prices, is solved; the shipped plan costs no more than the one-run or all-off challenger at equal feasibility.
scenarios.sensitivity: S1: the multi-start seed set in optimizer.py; one all-zero or all-energy set loses a basin.
scenarios.tradeoff: T1: each added start costs solve time on a Raspberry-Pi-class host (D9).

scenarios.scenario: price_risk_lambda is above zero; predicted cost, baseline, savings and the price tiles equal the feed's prices times energy, and the premium moves only the objective.
scenarios.sensitivity: S2: the single prices array the solver hands both the objective and the result.
scenarios.tradeoff: T2: carrying two price series widens the result payload the card and the ledger read.

scenarios.scenario: A weather forecast stops advancing, a PV meter goes silent, or a push-mode flag is quiet for an hour; within one cycle the input is treated as stale, Input Problem tells the truth, and the plan falls back to the documented default.
scenarios.sensitivity: S3: the age rule per input kind (polled, on-change, forecast row).
scenarios.tradeoff: T3: a shorter age limit raises false Input Problem on healthy report-on-change devices (D14-s2-01).

scenarios.scenario: A stored document, an option or a live state carries NaN, a boolean, an absurd hour count or a year-1 timestamp; setup and every later cycle complete, the value is quarantined once and one record says so.
scenarios.sensitivity: S4: the finiteness and domain test at inputs.py and store.py.
scenarios.tradeoff: T4: a strict boundary rejects values an earlier release stored, which then needs a migration rather than a refusal.

scenarios.scenario: The solve worker's pipe breaks or Home Assistant stops mid-solve; the lock is released in bounded time and no repair issue outlives the next good solve.
scenarios.sensitivity: S5: _PROCESS_LOCK held across worker.wait().
scenarios.tradeoff: T5: a bounded wait can abandon a worker that is still alive and using memory (D9).

scenarios.scenario: Flow temperature rises by 10 K at fixed source temperature; scalar and batch COP both fall, by the same factor.
scenarios.sensitivity: S6: the Carnot factor exists twice in thermal_model.py.
scenarios.tradeoff: T6: correcting the scalar twin shifts every learned COP correction and golden fixture that absorbed the inverted law (claimed drift, learner re-convergence).

scenarios.scenario: A price sensor reports in a minor unit, or a tariff has weekday rules and a capacity charge; the plan's price vector, the fee vector and the billed peak equal a hand calculation for a known week.
scenarios.sensitivity: S7: the unit scale at inputs.py and the day index in grid_fee.py.
scenarios.tradeoff: T7: the fix changes published money for existing installs at upgrade; the release notes owe the step first.

scenarios.scenario: An unplanned hot-water charge, an away week or a load-limited ceiling probe occurs; no house or capacity learner ingests the interval, and a genuine internal gain is recovered within its stated band.
scenarios.sensitivity: S8: the freeze predicate, today split between the coordinator and each learner.
scenarios.tradeoff: T8: a wider freeze slows learning on installs with few clean intervals.

scenarios.scenario: The user selects Off, the plan goes stale on an idle step, or the entry is unloaded or removed; every entity the optimizer wrote reads its pre-optimizer value within one cycle, and a failed restore is retried.
scenarios.sensitivity: S9: restore ownership; four writers have no owner at the fork.
scenarios.tradeoff: T9: restoring on a stale plan hands the pump back sooner, giving up the hold a short forecast outage would have kept.

scenarios.scenario: A step boundary passes between two solves; frequency, displace, curve offset and the disinfection switch follow the step covering now, not the step the last solve cut.
scenarios.sensitivity: S10: the one rule for the step covering now, written four times.
scenarios.tradeoff: T10: re-cutting the action between solves adds writes against the daily write budget and compressor wear.

scenarios.scenario: A target is off the entity's step, above its max, or the entity is unavailable; the write is quantised to the entity's grid and range or not made, and never recorded as made.
scenarios.sensitivity: S11: the arbiter's held record, which both suppresses repeat writes and decides release.
scenarios.tradeoff: T11: reading the entity before each write costs a state read per actuator per cycle and can chase a pump's own echo (the 20 s echo grace).

scenarios.scenario: A rule with several copies changes (water heat capacity, the covering step, the evidence cap); the change is one edit at one owner and an agreement test fails if a copy returns.
scenarios.sensitivity: S12: duplication_copies 18, shape_copies 40 and layer_violations 13 at the fork.
scenarios.tradeoff: T12: a shared helper adds an import edge; done carelessly it raises layer_violations or seam_cut_total while lowering the clone count.

scenarios.scenario: A fixer adds a cycle step to coordinator.py; the structure ratchet prices the growth whether it lands inside the class or beside it.
scenarios.sensitivity: S13: max_class_loc and class_excess_loc see class spans only; 2,980 lines sit outside.
scenarios.tradeoff: T13: a new ratchet row at zero headroom blocks unrelated fixes on the hot file until someone pays.

scenarios.scenario: A user presses a what-if three times in a second while the fuse advisor is due; at most one extra solve is in flight, the main solve is not delayed past its interval, and nothing runs a thermostat simulation on the event loop.
scenarios.sensitivity: S14: the solve budget and in-flight guard at the cycle seam.
scenarios.tradeoff: T14: a strict budget delays or refuses a user's what-if answer (D4).

scenarios.scenario: The card stays open for a week; retained history rows stay within the 48 h span.
scenarios.sensitivity: S15: HistorySource.absorb has no trim.
scenarios.tradeoff: T15: trimming forces a re-fetch when the user scrolls back past the span.

scenarios.scenario: A one-zone house, an on/off compressor, a pump with no heating-only mode and an install with no hot water are set up with defaults; model, plan views, entities and advisor each describe that plant and no other.
scenarios.sensitivity: S16: the plant-shape predicates (two-zone, modulating, has hot water) and their defaults.
scenarios.tradeoff: T16: changing the default of two_zone_mode moves the plan of every install that never set it.

scenarios.scenario: A Fahrenheit install writes a set-point; the written value converts back to the Celsius the plan chose.
scenarios.sensitivity: S17: TEMPERATURE_UNIT_TO_C and its two readers in inputs.py.
scenarios.tradeoff: T17: none found; the inverse is exact.

scenarios.scenario: A user reconfigures an entry after saving options, or changes the weekday comfort value while keeping the weekend one; the saved entry holds exactly what the form showed.
scenarios.sensitivity: S18: settings stored in entry.data and entry.options, merged by every reader.
scenarios.tradeoff: T18: moving 41 settings to options needs a config-entry migration that a downgrade cannot undo.

scenarios.scenario: A press or an action is refused or given an unparseable argument; the caller gets a translated error, and energy meters carry the state class the statistics engine needs.
scenarios.sensitivity: S19: off_the_action returns before the outcome exists.
scenarios.tradeoff: T19: awaiting the outcome holds the service call open for the length of a solve.

scenarios.quality: usability and text truth (D4, D5, D6)
scenarios.scenario: A German or Swedish user on a phone removes a pipe, reads a stale-plan tooltip and a failure line; the target is at least 24 px, every placeholder is filled and no English is spliced in.
scenarios.sensitivity: S20: card rules written beside the token scales (card_rule_copies 70).
scenarios.tradeoff: T20: larger hit bands overlap neighbouring pipes in dense layouts.

scenarios.quality: usability and text truth (D4, D5, D6)
scenarios.scenario: A reader compares a number in README.md, docs/ or strings.json with the constant that decides it (legionella interval, input age, echo grace, wood packing); they agree, and the fact has one home.
scenarios.sensitivity: S21: prose numbers no check derives from code.
scenarios.tradeoff: T21: generating or pinning text ties every default change to a text and translation change in the same pull request.

scenarios.quality: usability and text truth (D4, D5, D6)
scenarios.scenario: A reader follows a path or name cited in a comment or policy file; it resolves at the fork, and no sentence runs past 40 words.
scenarios.sensitivity: S22: no detector for prose paths or sentence length.
scenarios.tradeoff: T22: rewriting about 2,200 long sentences in production and tests touches every hot file and collides with each behaviour group, so it lands last.

scenarios.scenario: A merge reaches main while a gate run at that head is red, or a live ruleset changes; a detector reports it within one sweep.
scenarios.sensitivity: S23: counts.mjs reads one of three rulesets; the gate context is published by several runs.
scenarios.tradeoff: T23: the fix is instrument work, frozen until round 12; the exposure stays open for the round.

scenarios.scenario: A reviewer blocks a pull request or a fixer records friction; the class word resolves to one vocabulary and one policy file.
scenarios.sensitivity: S24: two writers of the block vocabulary and a free-form friction id.
scenarios.tradeoff: T24: a closed vocabulary refuses a genuinely new class until someone extends it.

scenarios.scenario: The coordinator changes how it stores its mode or another private value; no collaborator module is edited, because each received the value as an argument or read it from a published view.
scenarios.sensitivity: S25: collaborators handed the coordinator itself (boost.py, diagnostics.py, pump_arbiter.py).
scenarios.tradeoff: T25: handing values widens call signatures; past ten parameters it needs a value object.

scenarios.scenario: A fixer breaks the path from a rendered form error to the corrected submit, or doubles the solves in one coordinator cycle; a script of the gate fails.
scenarios.sensitivity: S26: flow tests stop at the error (51 of 53 rendered errors) and the stress gate runs no coordinator cycle and probes 6 of 54 scenarios for memory.
scenarios.tradeoff: T26: each added lane costs gate minutes on every scoped run that reaches it.

scenarios.scenario: The quantity a ratchet row names grows through another spelling (const read through a module binding, a rule written twice in one function, an import nothing loads, lines beside the class); the row moves.
scenarios.sensitivity: S27: rows keyed on one spelling of the thing they count.
scenarios.tradeoff: T27: a repaired row that reads higher is a budget raise, which waits for the owner's confirmation.

scenarios.scenario: A month has one settled interval, or the install has no hot water; a sensor that cannot yet know its value is unavailable or bounded, and its availability and its value come from one predicate.
scenarios.sensitivity: S28: availability and value decided in two places (the open-month projection, the gap advisor's hot-water test).
scenarios.tradeoff: T28: a minimum coverage holds back a figure the user expects on the first day of the month.

scenarios.scenario: A sensor's state class, device class or name is corrected; statistics accept it, and no entity id changes without a registry migration.
scenarios.sensitivity: S29: metadata written beside the value and never compared with it.
scenarios.tradeoff: T29: a corrected class or name on a published entity can break the continuity of its long-term statistics.

scenarios.scenario: A class with a barrier from an earlier round returns in another spelling (an unlatched .exception, forecast row 0 read as now, an off-grid selector in services.yaml); the barrier refuses it.
scenarios.sensitivity: S30: barriers that match one syntactic shape of the class.
scenarios.tradeoff: T30: a wider barrier refuses sound code until the site joins the reasoned list.

scenarios.scenario: A fix for one instance of a class merges; the class's sweep over every seam reads no instance left at the stamp.
scenarios.sensitivity: S31: a class spans seams, and each seam's group fixes only its own instances.
scenarios.tradeoff: T31: sweeping every seam per class costs seat hours no single finding asked for.

scenarios.scenario: A user's diagnostics bundle is loaded; every document a writer stored is admitted by its loader, and a debug row with an unpriced sample is kept.
scenarios.sensitivity: S32: store.DOMAINS declares less than the writers write.
scenarios.tradeoff: T32: a wider schema admits documents an earlier release wrote wrongly (T4).

scenarios.scenario: An analyst reads the solver self-test and the learner state from the bundle; a restart that ran no solve is not counted as a solve, and a learner's stored evidence survives the restart that wrote it.
scenarios.sensitivity: S33: values published before the cycle that produces them has run.
scenarios.tradeoff: T33: withholding a not-yet-run value leaves the entity unknown for the first cycle after every restart.

scenarios.scenario: A user calls set_thermal_parameters on a two-zone house, answers quick setup's wood questions, or calls run_optimization; the plan moves as the field's description says, or the call is refused with the reason.
scenarios.sensitivity: S34: a feature whose effect depends on a plant condition its own surface does not state.
scenarios.tradeoff: T34: refusing a call that was accepted and inert breaks automations that send it.

scenarios.scenario: A user configures an outdoor temperature sensor or restores a learned snapshot; the reading reaches the plan, and the restore picks a snapshot that carried accuracy evidence.
scenarios.sensitivity: S35: a configured input or a stored record that no later step reads.
scenarios.tradeoff: T35: a measured outdoor value joined to the forecast moves the first plan step of every install that has the sensor.

scenarios.scenario: Home Assistant stops or the entry unloads with background tasks pending; the shutdown waits for them, capped at 5 s, and then the task set is empty whether or not every task finished.
scenarios.sensitivity: S36: the task set is written in place by _spawn, by every task's done-callback and by the shutdown's clear. Only the clear is in an async method, and no await follows it.
scenarios.tradeoff: T36: a task that outlives the capped wait runs on untracked. Dropping the clear would keep it tracked and leave the set non-empty after shutdown; cancelling it instead could cut a store save short.

groups.architect_note: The kernel's owners and their readers: plan_step owns "the step covering now" with its half-open end rule, read by the coordinator, the arbiter and both planned-room copies; water heat capacity, a naive instant's zone and the finite test get one definition each in const.py and drift.py; the two evidence-note methods share drift.py's owner. D7-s1-05 is kept here with its note and step arms; each other arm is carried by the group of the seam that owns the rule (entity-service, money, learners, actuation-release, inputs-freshness), and the finding closes when the last arm has merged. 3 findings (0 merged in), size M; class tags N-duplicated-rule, N-no-expiry, P2. Plan: ADR-001 is this group's approved design. It is the prerequisite of R11-SEAM-actuation-writes and R11-SEAM-inputs-freshness, which read the step owner. Refused shapes: two bodies folded under one function with nothing shared, and a helper handed a detector's list.

What the pure layer offers its importers: utc_elapsed_seconds is imported from drift.py, its owner, HISTORY_LENGTH moves to const.py, and currency.py imports HomeAssistant for its annotation only, so the pure modules that reached Home Assistant through accuracy.py and currency.py stop doing so. The reader's clock, the design ADR-002 part 2 gives four of the six modules D7-s1-06 left open, is carried by R11-SEAM-inputs-freshness in inputs.py; setpoint_check and snapshots stay. 1 finding (0 merged in), size S; class tags N-leaf-imports-solver. Plan: ADR-002 parts 1 and 3 are this group's approved design. No edge in or out, and no edit in coordinator.py.

groups.seam: no owning seam (deletion in the module that holds the state)
groups.architect_note: State production stores and nothing reads (D7-s3-05): constants named only by tests, parameters a function never loads, locals, attributes and fields only tests read, each deleted in the module that holds it and at its callers, and the fourteen import bindings D7-s1-03 lists. No owner is created or moved and no behaviour changes, so this one group is cut by kind of edit and not by seam; COMPONENTS.md states the deviation. 1 finding (0 merged in), size M; class tags N-structure-blind. Plan: ADR-001 part 4. It is the prerequisite of R11-SEAM-ratchets, which records the import row at the value these deletions leave. A parameter a caller still computes is removed at the caller too; a field a stored document carries is left.

Physical laws and the plant shape: the scalar Carnot factor agrees with its batch twin, delivery and derate keep their sign, and one predicate each answers "two zones", "modulating" and "has hot water" for the model, the plan views, the options page and the action. 11 findings (0 merged in), size L; class tags N-table-value, N-wrong-law, P2. Plan: ADR-008 is the approved design of the predicate work; the law fixes are point fixes. The has-hot-water predicate becomes a public function with the gap advisor as a new reader; the fall in private_cross_module is banked only when the reviewer finds that reader in the PR. Golden drift from the Carnot fix is claimed with its direction.

Every value entering through inputs.py is scaled once and tested finite and in domain: the minor-unit price scale, the Fahrenheit inverse, boolean and timestamp parsers, numeric options. The P1 sweep enumerator is the fitness function. 6 findings (0 merged in), size M; class tags N-missing-unit-scale, P1, P8. Plan: no edit in coordinator.py. D1-s3-02, whose parser lives there, is carried by R11-SEAM-inputs-freshness of the same seam, so the price-scale fix waits on no coordinator slot.

Age and expiry of live inputs: a forecast that stopped advancing, a silent PV meter, forecast row 0 read as now, push-mode flags aged on a polling limit, and the measured outdoor value joining the forecast series. The end rule is the kernel's step owner, hence the edge from R11-SEAM-kernel-step. 7 findings (0 merged in), size M; class tags N-dead-input, N-no-expiry, N-staleness, P1, P2. Plan: it also carries the reader arm of D7-s1-05 (ADR-001) and the reader's clock of ADR-002 part 2, which leaves inputs.py with no Home Assistant import, and D1-s3-02, a guard finding of this seam whose one edit is in coordinator.py.

store.DOMAINS is the one schema: writers and loaders agree with it, non-finite leaves are quarantined, and a restored value is tested before it is applied. 5 findings (0 merged in), size M; class tags N-silent-zero, P1, P2.

Prices, fees, capacity windows and the ledger: whole-payload parse, weekday index, highest-window aggregate, scalar and batch top-k agreeing, open-window projection with a floor on settled time, one currency owner for the plan and the options dialog. 9 findings (0 merged in), size L; class tags I4, I5, N-inverted-aggregate, N-partial-payload-parse, N-partial-window-extrapolation, P2, P7, P8. Plan: ADR-006. The exact top-k takes the largest, as its batch twin does; the smooth scalar becomes one row of its batch only if golden fixtures stay byte-identical and the solve-time harness does not regress, else that part is dropped and recorded. It also carries the day and entry arms of D7-s1-05: price_model.py's usable day and ledger.py's month entry each get one owner (ADR-001).

Start set brackets the all-off and wood-covered optima; the risk premium stays in the objective and out of every published money figure; the slot label tie is ordered. Fitness: D0 race harnesses, mutation kill rate on optimizer.py, shape_copies. 4 findings (0 merged in), size M; class tags N-objective-as-money, N-unordered-tiebreak, P4.

One freeze predicate owns which interval a learner may ingest (away, unplanned charge, load-limited probe, charge-start dip); the sysid adoption interval covers quantised readings. After the plant model: its law fixes move the residual every learner fits. 8 findings (0 merged in), size L; class tags I5, N-confounded-learner, N-event-misattribution, P5. Plan: ADR-008 (one freeze predicate) is the approved design; ADR-003 moves the identification switch from a per-cycle store on the collaborator to an argument of the arm call. It also carries the fdjac arm of D7-s1-05: sysid.py's forward-difference Jacobian gets one owner (ADR-001).

One restore owner for every entity the optimizer writes: supply switch, frequency, valve, circulation, mode and tank set-point are handed back on Off, stale plan, unload and remove, with a retried restore and a load that completes before the first read. 6 findings (0 merged in), size L; class tags N-order-coupling, N-restore-race, N-unreleased-hold. Plan: ADR-004 is the approved design. The circulation pumps' write, record and restore move to one owner object registered with off_restore; the pinned check that Off writes nothing else is re-pinned to the 2026-11-15 ruling in the same PR. It also carries the notice arm of D7-s1-05, legionella.py's interval notice (ADR-001), as the actuation seam's first group on that file. The circ term (shared_inplace_writes 3 to 2 and its six coord_footprint statements) is banked only when the PR registers the real restoring owner with off_restore.py, the one that restores on Off, stale plan, unload and remove; a class that only holds the dict is metric-gamed and banks nothing (decided 2026-11-18, orchestrator under mandate, pending owner confirmation).

What is written and when: every actuator reads the step covering now from the kernel owner, values sit on the entity's grid and range, a write to an unavailable entity is not recorded, the lead mode is checked against the entity. After release: both use the arbiter's held record. 9 findings (0 merged in), size L; class tags N-mode-coupled-write, N-stale-step-actuation, N-step-grid, P11, P2, P3. Plan: reads the covering step from plan_step (ADR-001) and the held record as ADR-004 leaves it.

The cycle owns when a solve runs: a write during an in-flight refresh arms a trailing run, every solve request shares one in-flight guard and budget, the worker's failure arms are bounded, and the action and the button reach one refresh path. 8 findings (0 merged in), size L; class tags N-dropped-refresh, N-solve-recompute, N-unbudgeted-background, N-uncleared-issue, P10, P2. Plan: no ADR fixes the shape of the one in-flight guard and budget; designer.md is dispatched before the fixer.

How a failure is reported: persist failures surface once above DEBUG, broad handlers leave a record, the generic arm is latched, an unparseable service argument raises, the context is write-once, the coordinator carries the typed entry and the strict-typing row is re-measured. 7 findings (0 merged in), size M; class tags I5, N-log-flood, N-shared-config, N-silent-zero, N-swallowed-failure. Plan: ADR-003 (both writers of the shared optimization config publish a replaced context) and ADR-008 (away owns the return-time parser as a public function, read by the service, the coordinator and the datetime entity). The fall in private_cross_module is banked only when the reviewer finds the service's new call in the PR. Acceptance check for ADR-003's stale holders: early_cutoff.arm stores the handed OptimizationConfig in held.wiring (CutoffInputs); after a comfort-weight or target change publishes a replaced context, the held cutoff reads the new values, not the old ones, before the next cycle re-arms; a test pins it (decided 2026-11-18, orchestrator under mandate, pending owner confirmation).

One place for a setting: options-flow settings leave entry.data by a versioned migration, so reconfigure, the options save and the reader agree; the weekend value survives a weekday change; the pre-fill pages render their placeholders and store only settings. 6 findings (1 merged in), size L; class tags I4, N-dead-input, N-entry-data-placement, P2. Plan: the entry migration cannot be undone by a downgrade (tradeoff T18); designer.md is dispatched before the fixer, and the release notes owe the step first.

Published metadata and outcomes: state_class and device_class match the value, a refused press raises, availability and value share a predicate, selectors sit on their grid. D8-s2-02 changes no entity id without a registry migration. 8 findings (0 merged in), size M; class tags N-entity-metadata, N-name-sort, N-silent-zero, N-step-grid, P2. Plan: It also carries the avail arm of D7-s1-05: the three available properties that gate on one payload flag take entity.py's one owner (ADR-001).

Size L with no approved design: a design is owed (designer.md) before the fixer (decided 2026-11-18, orchestrator under mandate, pending owner confirmation).

User-facing strings state what the code does after this round's behaviour groups have merged; placeholders match across languages; copy style is one convention. Verified against the text ledger. 7 findings (1 merged in), size M; class tags I4, I5, N-copy-style. Plan: ADR-010.

What the suite exercises: a flow test follows each rendered error to its recovery, the coverage register row states the measured tier, the stress memory channel probes every scenario and one lane drives coordinator cycles. 4 findings (0 merged in), size L; class tags I1, I5. Plan: no ADR; point additions to the suite. No edge: nothing here waits on another group. Size L with no approved design: a design is owed (designer.md) before the fixer (decided 2026-11-18, orchestrator under mandate, pending owner confirmation).

Ratchet rows and barriers that see what they name: a rule written twice in one function, a package import nothing loads, and an unlatched .exception or .critical log site. Each new row is recorded at its measured value when the group merges; no edge waits on R11-SEAM-dead-state, whose later deletions re-record the import row downward (the edge dropped, decided 2026-11-18, orchestrator under mandate, pending owner confirmation). 3 findings (0 merged in), size M; class tags N-log-flood, N-structure-blind. Plan: ADR-009. No function the architecture score reads from tests/structure.py changes; D7-s1-02 gets a row of its own beside duplicate_clones, and the score's clone census is not edited in this round. No budget is raised here.

The two rows whose value the owner sets: const fan-out read through a module binding (the corrected row reads 4 against a budget of 3) and module lines outside the class, whose limit the owner chooses. Cut from the other ratchet rows so the owner's confirmation holds only these two findings. 2 findings (0 merged in), size S; class tags N-structure-blind. Plan: ADR-009 part 2. The owner's confirmation is obtained before the branch is pushed. No edge: each row is recorded at the value measured when the owner confirms it, and a later merge that lowers it re-records the row downward.

Reader docs carry each fact once and the number the code holds; verified last, after every user-facing change. 12 findings (1 merged in), size L; class tags I5, N-comment-style, N-orphan-doc. Plan: ADR-010.

Policy and programme prose with a false or unresolvable sentence. Policy files merge serially on the owner's approving review; no instrument code changes here. 10 findings (3 merged in), size M; class tags I4, I5, N-move-stale-path. Plan: ADR-010.

A sentence-length count recorded as a ratchet lets it be paid per file. 2 findings (1 merged in), size XL; class tags I5, N-comment-style. Plan: ADR-010. No edge: the order against the behaviour groups is a hot-file order. The fixer cuts it into parts by seam, one PR per part; the part for a file is released when the last group in that file's row of PLAN.md's hot-file order has merged, and files no other group names are released at the first dispatch. The card's script is released after R11-SEAM-card and R11-SEAM-product-text.

Text only. 4 findings (6 merged in), size XL; class tags I5, N-comment-style, N-move-stale-path. Plan: ADR-010. No edge: last on each test file by the hot-file order, cut into parts the same way.
